did_you_know.text: The verse addresses “all nations” and “all peoples,” presenting the call to praise the Lord as a universal one.
The verse contains two verbs of praise—“Praise” and “Extol”—emphasizing the invitation to recognize the Lord’s greatness and proclaim his praise.
The phrases “all nations” and “all peoples” form a parallelism: two corresponding expressions describing every nation.
The opening verse is a direct command: the nations are called not only to acknowledge the Lord, but also to praise and extol him.
The word “For” connects the call to praise with its reason: the Lord’s steadfast love toward us is strong, and his faithfulness endures forever.
The phrase “his steadfast love toward us is strong” describes the Lord’s love as powerful, evident, and influential for those speaking on behalf of the community.
The words “forever” emphasize the eternal nature of the Lord’s faithfulness, not merely its existence at a particular time.
The psalm concludes with the words “Praise the Lord,” so the call to praise appears both at its beginning and at its end.
